[h3] Overall a pretty good game. It doesn't compare to the trilogy, but on sale, it's definitely worth getting and playing through. Probably a better introduction to the series than ME1 due to how dated that game is honestly. [/h3]

Lack of quicksave and quickload really is a huge downgrade, I dunno why they'd stop doing those in such a game where if you're like me, you want to quicksave a lot for dialogue because I regret my choices sometimes xD 
Difficulty wise, playing on insanity it's pretty annoying if you're put back 5-10 minutes after dying, especially if you're dying a lot. Oooor when you mess up near the end of killing an architect and you get to do the "fun" repetitive fighting for another 10-15 minutes.. (there are too many architect fights). It wasn't too bad overall for me, as 80-90% of the fights were quite easy, start of the game was a bit challenging however.

Something a bit annoying is that the console button is the same as my steam overlay button, which keeps bugging the game out when I accidentally press it, and no way of re-binding it. Have to restart the game to fix it after pressing it, or turn off steam overlay in-game (but that means no steam achievement notifications or screenshots which sucks too)

Lots of different guns which I like, though the research system means that you're not really able to get most of the guns at high levels to try a bunch of different ones. Personally I stick to something that works and just use it for most of the game, so it wasn't a huge issue for me, but it could be better for sure. would be really cool to have at least a shooting range deal where you can just test a gun instead of reading the stats. Something like the dhan shotgun forexample, that shoots a big fireball thingy which I didn't even know till one dropped near the end of the game, probably would've used that more if I had known.. assumed all shotguns were just normal shotguns.

I like the skills and how you can just reset them as much as you want, you could in ME2 and 3 as well, but you couldn't change your class without using a third party save editor. This game is a lot more flexible, though it does make your character a bit of a "john supersoldier" how you can just change between them a bunch (plus you can also literally change profiles which are basically classes from the trilogy mid-fight, because you're just so special and cool and amazing and-)

A big difference between this and the older ME games is how you can do big jumps and dashes with your jump pack, which makes combat a lot faster and overall more fun I'd say. In the older ones, you'd just be moving from cover to cover and sitting still a lot more. You can also hover in the air while shooting and using biotics etc which is cool. When I first played through all the games a few years ago, I was just using normal combat skills to begin with, and when I started my second playthroughs recently I switched to using biotics/tech stuff. Overall they definitely felt jank in ME1, a bit better in ME2, but a lot more fun to use in ME3 and andromeda.

One huuge downside with andromeda, is the lack of races in vs the trilogy, sure there are some new ones in this one, but I do miss a lot of the races from the trilogy. It's also a bit crap how they tease you at the end of andromeda that the quarians are coming or something, and then they just gave up with the game after it came out I guess?

I noticed that in a lot of the dialogue in andromeda, characters actually use the protagonist's first name (Sara or Scott) unlike the trilogy, which is pretty cool. (Also a few f bombs here and there in dialogue, I miss it when every game didn't have to be so damn PC, lol)
Plus having played a few different newer single player story games in the last year or so, it's SO nice to have the protagonist voiced instead of just mute.

Many fast travel points which is really nice, forward bases you put down when exploring places. I've always liked that system in games where it's pretty open world-y, like fallout / skyrim. Explore a place, then unlock it to fast travel back to there. Though I did find myself going back and forth a lot, despite trying to do all the quests on one planet, then the next, as some quests make you go to different planets. And it does get a bit annoying due to the unskippable cutscenes and such. Even when skipping, going to all the different planets to scan them takes forever too, think it was ME1 actually where it was super quick to do, then you got little cutscenes with the relays etc in 2 and 3. I have a mod that skips cutscenes for andromeda, yet I feel like I still watched a LOT of them. It's like the fallout 4 / 76 power armour animation.. sick as hell for a while, then.. you're sick OF it xD

Speaking of the open world type exploration, there are a good few puzzles which I really wasn't a huge fan of. I think there were 2 I literally had to search up, which made me think of when I played a bit of the new tomb raider games. It's not for everyone I guess :p
I also probably used like 10-15 encryption keys as I just didn't really find the time spent on those very rewarding once they got harder and took longer to do. The mining minigame too I just skipped outright with a mod that gets all the resources in one go at mining sites, similar to mods for the trilogy that lets you get all the resources from a specific spot with one probe etc.

No micromanaging of crew at all in terms of gear, which I sorta like, but after playing ME3 on insanity recently, I do miss garrus absolutely annihilating enemies with the typhoon lmao. also I only really used the manual control of their abilities in ME2 as that game was pretty damn hard. honestly I just realised at nearly 50 hours in andromeda that I can't even use their abilities manually, so.. guess that's how much I've missed that side of the game xD

But I gotta say, the teammates in andromeda do feel really useless most of the time on insanity, at best they draw aggro and sometimes do decent damage (especially against armoured enemies) with their abilties. But I'm most likely doing at least 70-80% of the overall damage. The crew are pretty cool too, plenty of dialogue between them while you're driving around, if anything I wish they'd talk more often so I could hear more of the dialogue with all the different people.
